sections.title: The Kings of the North and South
observations: Daniel 11 begins with a detailed prophecy concerning the conflicts between the kings of the North and the South, which are generally understood to represent the Seleucid and Ptolemaic empires, respectively.

This section outlines a series of battles and political maneuvers that characterize the historical interactions between these two powers, emphasizing the sovereignty of God over the affairs of nations.

sections.title: The Rise of a Notable King
observations: The narrative shifts to the rise of a powerful king, often interpreted as Antiochus IV Epiphanes, who exemplifies the hostility against the people of God.
His actions, including the desecration of the temple and persecution of the Jews, serve as a foreshadowing of future tribulations faced by God's people.

sections.title: The End Times and the Final Conflict
observations: The chapter concludes with a prophetic vision of a final conflict involving a king who will exalt himself above all, often associated with the Antichrist figure.
This section emphasizes the ultimate victory of God's people and the resurrection of the righteous, providing hope amidst the trials and tribulations.

importantVerses.commentary: Forces from him will arise and desecrate the sanctuary, doing away with the regular sacrifice and setting up the abomination of desolation.
He will seduce with flattery those who violate the covenant, but the people who know their God will be strong and take action.

questions: What does the conflict between the kings of the North and South reveal about God's sovereignty in history?
How do the events described in Daniel 11 relate to the New Testament teachings on the end times?
In what ways can we apply the lessons from the persecution faced by the Jews during Antiochus IV's reign to our own lives today?
